item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
There's a lot in here that I like, but a lot in here that I strenuously don't.

On the plus side, many specific details were quite cool, the most memorable being

The interior of the station itself is impossible to access due to an absence of Fifthist Church bullshit.

I definitely enjoyed the ending to the story, with Station27 taking the complete wrong assessment of Canine's character (at least to my reading.) Whatever in the hell 27 was up to is also pretty neat.

What I really, really dislike is the lolrandom nature of the bigger text blocks. In #Xipunia, the text was all pretty comprehensible and plainly written, even though it defined new and strange beings. It wasn't otherworldly because it threw in random words and phrases, it was otherworldly because it used very familiar internet style to convey more than one truly strange other world.

The links out absolutely did not convey dream-logic, especially given that you're basically linking from an imaginary dream internet to parts of the real internet.
The spastic language also really didn't help convey anything. Maybe if you were going for a mad AI who could only use internet references and couldn't quite speak English (or were writing a Daveyoufool skip), it would fit, but that's not dream-logic.

Surrealism mimics the structure and logic of dreams, with its strange transitions and associations. A lot of this feels like the conceptual equivalent of slapping the keys on a keyboard. Given that tonal failure, this feels like a really underwhelming use of the OW format. -1

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: I don't understand what people are talking about with this being illegible and incoherent. This has a coherent story and characters and arc.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I, on the other hand, have always hated incomprehensibility. Obfuscating your story with tons of gibberish is a really great way to make me dislike your story.

The problem with writing stories that emulate dreams is that dreams don't have narrative cohesion. They're random mish-mashes of images with no logic or consistency behind them. And while that may be interesting, it doesn't make a good story.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
After the MTF contest, I wondered if #Xiupania was a lightning-strike sort of article, something that works fantastically once but then fails a bit when future articles use the same format. However, I'm happy to say that this document is a pretty sweet piece of work — it's all that classic Oneiroi dream logic that combines numbers stations, conspiracy theories, and ARGs to create something that feels very right.

If I could select an issue, I would say that it might have been even better to include formats that had not already been seen in #Xiupania. At the very least, I would encourage that for other people seeking to make articles in this format: let's not allow something so fresh and weird to become stale by reusing the same code snippets in everything.

Other than that, though, this is solid.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
On the one hand, I'm not a huge fan of Oneiroi, but this isn't terrible. The format is hard to read, but the little parts of it are amusing and interesting. Though, fact that this is essentially documents an overly-long ARG kind of hits a bit close to home as someone who had to wait literally six months from the start of an ARG to the finish for Overwatch. Sombra was worth it, though.

Overall, neutral-vote.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
There's something about Oneiroi articles that I find almost seductive. The way it's presented is so far deviated from the standard go-around here, and the subject matter is almost alien. It's very easy to find yourself engrossed in the story, and still unsure of what you experienced when it's over.

I don't feel like an Oneiroi article is acceptable, to me, without that feeling. The sense of drifting and uncertainty. Of something and someplace that is, and very much isn't.

Fortunately, this hits all of those points. A delightful read.

item.title: YES OH MY GOD YES THIS IS ALL I EVER WANTED OUT OF ONEIROI
item.content:encoded:
Specifically I love that it is this kind of dream logic that makes a terrible amount of sense with a looming idea that shit is happening but the conclusion that ends the tension of "What is it" provides even more "WHAT IS IT"!

this thing makes me feel very strongly about it
